newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Zinc treatment fee seen off slightly in 1996.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Zinc treatment fee seen off slightly in 1996.

text.p: Zinc smelting and refining charges in 1997 could fall short of 1996 levels due to a growing surplus of concentrates, although the fall likely to be less than some miners are hoping for, industry sources said on Monday.
Based on what smelters can afford, charges for processing intermediate zinc concentrates into metal form may fetch as much as US$185.00 a tonne, basis US$1,000 a tonne, the sources said.
The price range is below the US$190.00 a tonne agreed to by miners and smelters for 1996.
But it would represent a substantial premium on the US$155.000 a tonne some mining companies are aiming for in opening round talks with the important Japanese smelting pool consortium.
The negotiated terms hold strong implications for Australia's two leading zinc producers, MIM Holdings Ltd and Pasminco Ltd, which regularly ship material to Asia for smelting.
The talks typically conclude in February, but it is not unusual for negotiations to drag on for a further month or two, particularly if the sides are far apart.
"The smelters realise its a different market now, but I don't think they would be willing to go much under US$180.00," a buyer of zinc concentrates for an Asian smelter told Reuters.
Mining companies have entered annual "mating season" talks with smelting companies armed with a list of production curtailments, which bolster arguments for a reduction in fees.

One of the most formidable weapons in the miners' camp is the planned suspension of zinc mining at Canada's Anvil Range Faro zinc and lead mine in the Yukon Territory for three months from December 20 due to weak metals prices.
Some uncertainty over levels of mine production from deposits in Ireland and Morroco also are contributing to perceptions that supplies are tight.
As concentrate supplies decline, smelters are forced to become more competitive for business from the mines.
Most zinc concentrates exported from Australia are smelted in Japan and Korea.
